documents.title: Twin Primes in the Wheel Lattice: Structure, Density, and the Period–Window Dichotomy

references.text: Brun (1919), sieve + convergence of sum 1/q over twins
Selberg parity example; Bombieri asymptotic sieve

nodes.name: Pair Lattice S_k^(2)
nodes.statement: The pair lattice S_k^(2) is the set of residues r mod P_k such that gcd(r(r+2), P_k) = 1.

representation.content: S_k^{(2)} = { r mod P_k : gcd(r(r+2), P_k) = 1 }

sources.heading: 1. Notation
sources.quote: S_k^{(2)} the pair lattice: { r mod P_k : gcd(r(r+2), P_k) = 1 }

nodes.name: TP0: One-Way Containment of Twin Primes in the Pair Lattice
nodes.statement: For every k and x, the count of primes q ≤ x with q, q+2 both prime and q > p_k is at most the count of q ≤ x with q mod P_k in S_k^(2); equality holds on q in [p_{k+1}, p_{k+1}^2 - 2) and, in general, nowhere else.
nodes.formal: \#\{ q \le x : q, q+2 \text{ prime}, q>p_k\} \le \#\{ q \le x : q \bmod P_k \in S_k^{(2)} \}

sources.heading: 2. Two objects: classes and integers
sources.quote: Equality holds on q ∈ [p_{k+1}, p_{k+1}² − 2) and, in general, nowhere else.

nodes.name: TP0 Rough Half, Kernel-Checked
nodes.statement: The rough-half of TP0's containment (a twin prime pair is a pair of P_k-rough residues) is proved in Lean as Twin.rough_pair_of_twin.

sources.heading: 9. Claim → status table
sources.quote: rough half: `Twin.rough_pair_of_twin`

nodes.name: TP1: Pair Count Recursion
nodes.statement: T_1 = 1 and, for k ≥ 1 with p = p_{k+1}, T_{k+1} = (p − 2)·T_k, hence T_k equals the product of (p_i − 2) over odd primes p_i up to p_k.

nodes.name: TP1 Per-Prime Factor, Kernel-Checked
nodes.statement: Twin.pairLattice_prime and Twin.card_pairLattice_prime establish |S^(2) mod p| = p − 2 for every prime p ≥ 3 in Lean.

sources.heading: 4.1 The pair count recursion
sources.quote: `Twin.pairLattice_prime` identifies S^{(2)} mod p as `range p` minus `{0, p−2}`

nodes.name: Table of T_k, φ(P_k), τ_k for k = 1..8
nodes.statement: Exact computed values of T_k, φ(P_k), κ_k, and τ_k are tabulated for k=1 through k=8, e.g. T_6=1485, τ_6≈0.04945.

nodes.name: Machine-Checked T_k Values and Multiplier
nodes.statement: A Lean #eval reproduces the T_k column for k ≤ 6 and independently checks TP1's multiplier p_{k+1}−2 at the first three promotions.

nodes.name: TP2: Pair Lattice Recursion (Promotion)
nodes.statement: Under wheel promotion the pair lattice S_{k+1}^(2) is the union of p replicated copies of S_k^(2) minus two disjoint deletion sets D and D', each of size T_k, arising from twisted affine images of shifted pair lattices.

sources.heading: 4.2 The promotion (pair version of Claim F1)

nodes.name: TP3: Pair Lattice Density Equals the Singular Series
nodes.statement: The density τ_k of the pair lattice equals half of C_2(p_k) times the square of the product of (1-1/p) over odd primes up to p_k, and asymptotically τ_k ~ 2 C_2 e^{-2γ} / log^2 p_k.

sources.heading: 4.3 Density = the singular series
sources.quote: τ_k ~ 2 C_2 e^{−2γ} / log² p_k

nodes.name: TP3a: Hole Density Exceeds Prime Density by a Constant
nodes.statement: The wheel's single-hole survivor density exceeds the true prime density by the constant 2e^{-γ} ≈ 1.123, and squaring gives the pair lattice density exceeding the conjectured twin prime density by a factor (2e^{-γ})^2 ≈ 1.2599.

sources.heading: 4.3 Density = the singular series
sources.quote: a factor (2e^{−γ})² ≈ 1.2599.

nodes.name: TP8: Deletion Geometry of Promotion
nodes.statement: In wheel promotion at prime p over previous primorial P, each class r is deleted at tile j0(r) = -r·P̄ (left hit) and j1(r) = -(r+2)·P̄ (right hit), the offset j1(r)-j0(r) ≡ δ_k = -2P̄ (mod p) is independent of r, no copy is ever deleted twice, the two deletion sets D and D' are translates of each other by δ_k·P, and surviving tiles form two cyclic arcs of length at least ⌈(p-2)/2⌉ consecutive copies.

sources.heading: 4.4 Deletion geometry: two strikes, rigidly linked
sources.quote: j_1(r) − j_0(r) ≡ −2P̄ =: δ_k (mod p), independent of r

nodes.name: TP8 (a)/(b) Kernel-Checked
nodes.statement: Twin.deleted_tiles_ne and Twin.deleted_tile_offset_eq formalize that no copy dies twice and that the offset δ_k is independent of the class r.

sources.heading: 4.4 Deletion geometry: two strikes, rigidly linked
sources.quote: (a) and (b) are formalised: `Twin.deleted_tiles_ne` / `Twin.deleted_tiles_ne_tile`

nodes.name: TP8a Adjacency Table for k=1..8
nodes.statement: The two deleted copies of a class are cyclically adjacent exactly when δ_k ≡ ±1 (mod p_{k+1}); this occurs at k=1 (vacuously) and k=3, and not at k=2,4,5,6,7,8 in the tabulated range.

sources.heading: Remark TP8a
sources.quote: The k = 3 row is explicit: mod 210 every class loses copies j = 4 and j = 5.

nodes.name: TP4: Admissibility of General Patterns
nodes.statement: For a finite set H, the size of S_k^(H) is the product over i≤k of (p_i - ν_i) where ν_i is the number of residues mod p_i occupied by H, and S_k^(H) is nonempty for all k iff H is admissible (ν_i < p_i for all i).

nodes.name: TP5: Composite Pair-Holes Exist for k ≥ 4
nodes.statement: S_k^(2) contains classes whose small representatives are composite in one or both coordinates for k ≥ 4, since p_{k+1}-rough composites m,m+2 form pairs lying in S_k^(2), and such pairs exist below P_k once p_{k+1}^2 < P_k.

sources.heading: 5.1 Holes are candidates
sources.quote: S_k^{(2)} contains classes whose small representatives are composite in one or both coordinates

nodes.name: Example: Composite Pair-Hole (167,169)
nodes.statement: The pair (167,169) lies in S_4^(2): both coprime to 210, 167 is prime, 169 = 13^2 is composite, checked in Lean via Rough 11 167 ∧ Rough 11 169 ∧ ¬ Nat.Prime 169.

nodes.name: TP6: Period-Wide Counts Bound π_2 From Above
nodes.statement: By TP0, for every k and x, the count of twin-candidate positions ≤ x is an upper bound on π_2(x); growth of that count is compatible with π_2(x) being bounded.

sources.heading: 5.3 The inequality has a direction
sources.quote: Growth of that count from stage to stage is growth of an upper bound

nodes.name: TP-J: Pair Jacobsthal Bound
nodes.statement: The maximal gap g_2(P_k) between consecutive elements of the pair lattice mod P_k is conjectured to grow no faster than log^2 P_k, comparable to p_k^2.

sources.heading: 6. A sufficient window condition
sources.quote: Conjecture TP-J (pair Jacobsthal). g_2(P_k) ≪ log² P_k ≍ p_k².

nodes.name: Claim W: Window Occupancy
nodes.statement: For every prime p > 2 there exist h with p ≤ h, h+2 < p^2, and both h and h+2 coprime to P_{<p} (p-rough), i.e. the pair lattice at the stage below p has a hole-pair inside the certified window.

sources.heading: 6. A sufficient window condition
sources.quote: for every prime p > 2 there exist h with p ≤ h, h + 2 < p², and both h and h+2 coprime to P_{<p}

nodes.name: Twin.WindowAt and Twin.Window Lean Statements
nodes.statement: Twin.WindowAt p formalizes window occupancy for a single prime p, and Twin.Window quantifies it over primes; the unrestricted form is false at p=2 (Twin.not_windowAt_two).

sources.heading: 6. A sufficient window condition
sources.quote: Formalised as a statement: `Twin.WindowAt p` (single prime) and `Twin.Window` (the quantified claim).

nodes.name: TP7: Claim W Implies the Twin Prime Conjecture
nodes.statement: Claim W implies there are infinitely many twin primes, proved in Lean via Twin.infinite_twins_of_window using only prime_of_rough_of_lt_sq.

sources.heading: 6. A sufficient window condition
sources.quote: Claim W implies there are infinitely many twin primes.

nodes.name: TP7 Kernel-Checked Proof
nodes.statement: Twin.infinite_twins_of_window and Twin.exists_twin_ge are formalized in Lean, citing prime_of_rough_of_lt_sq alone and mentioning the promotion recursion nowhere.

sources.heading: 8.3 Formalisation status
sources.quote: `infinite_twins_of_window` cites `prime_of_rough_of_lt_sq` twice and nothing else from §4.

nodes.name: Claim O2/F3: Roughness Certifies Primality on the Window
nodes.statement: A wheel certifies primality only on the window [p_{k+1}, p_{k+1}^2), where holes are exactly primes; imported from paper.md as an external result used throughout this document.

sources.heading: 0. Summary
sources.quote: a wheel certifies primality only on the window [p_{k+1}, p_{k+1}²) (Claim O2/F3

nodes.name: Window Occupancy Computation via Twin.windowWitnesses
nodes.statement: Twin.windowWitnesses p enumerates all witnesses of WindowAt p for primes below 60, and the counts are compared to the period-wide density prediction τ·(p^2-p).

sources.heading: 6.1 Occupancy of the certified window, computed
sources.quote: `Twin.windowWitnesses p` enumerates every `h` witnessing `WindowAt p`

nodes.name: Window Occupancy Table for p < 60
nodes.statement: Claim W holds for every prime 2 < p < 60 with witness counts never below 2; p=2 is the sole failure; observed/predicted ratio stays in 0.66 to 1.19 with no systematic deficit visible at these sizes.

sources.heading: 6.1 Occupancy of the certified window, computed
sources.quote: W holds for every prime 2 < p < 60, with the witness count never below 2.

nodes.name: Claim W Is False at p = 2
nodes.statement: The unrestricted window claim fails at p=2 because the window [2,4) has no room for a pair at distance 2, formalized as Twin.not_windowAt_two; formalizing the prose changed it to quantify over p > 2.

sources.heading: 6. A sufficient window condition
sources.quote: the window of p = 2 is [2, 4), which has no room for a pair at distance 2 at all, so the unrestricted form is outright false

nodes.name: Equidistribution Gap Between Period-Wide Counts and Window Certification
nodes.statement: Converting a count over the full period P_k into occupancy of the window of relative length e^{-p_k} requires equidistribution of S_k^(2) at scale e^{-p_k}, an input the wheel recursion does not supply and modern sieve theory obtains only in averaged form.

sources.heading: 5.4 The bridging input is equidistribution
sources.quote: That is the input the modern literature works hardest for and obtains only in averaged form

nodes.name: Parity Problem Prevents Sieve Lower Bounds for Two-Variable Patterns
nodes.statement: The parity problem (Selberg's example; Bombieri's asymptotic sieve) shows a sieve of the shape used here cannot produce a positive lower bound separating 'both coordinates prime' from 'both coordinates have an odd number of prime factors'.

sources.heading: 5.3 The inequality has a direction
sources.quote: the parity problem (Selberg; Bombieri's asymptotic sieve) is the theorem-level statement that a sieve of this shape cannot produce a positive lower bound

nodes.name: Brun (1919)
nodes.statement: Brun's sieve gives π_2(x) ≪ x/log^2 x, and Brun's theorem shows convergence of Σ1/q over twins, exactly the shape TP1/TP3 predict.

nodes.statement: Goldston–Pintz–Yıldırım, Zhang's extension of Bombieri–Vinogradov, and Maynard–Tao/Polymath8 give bounded gaps (≤246) rather than gap 2, because the available equidistribution is lossy.

nodes.name: Iwaniec and Ford–Green–Konyagin–Maynard–Tao Jacobsthal Bounds
nodes.statement: Iwaniec's theorem g(P_k) ≪ log^2 P_k is the single-coordinate calibration for the pair Jacobsthal conjecture TP-J, and the FGKMT lower bound shows there is no slack to spare.

nodes.name: Free Twin Generator on Top of Algorithm B
nodes.statement: Algorithm B emits primes in increasing order with O(1) state, and twin detection is one extra register comparing consecutive emitted primes for a gap of 2, at no extra asymptotic cost, inheriting O(1) random-access restart.

representation.content: twins(): prev := none; for q in B(): if prev≠none and q−prev=2: emit (prev,q); prev := q

sources.heading: 8.1 A twin generator, free

nodes.name: Pair Wheel for Scan Restriction
nodes.statement: A pair wheel restricts scan positions to pairSpokes, the T_w of φ(W) spokes that are pair-relevant; at W=30030 this is 1485 of 5760 spokes, a 3.88x reduction in scan positions, but the saving applies only to the scan, not the advance, because pair-restricting the advance requires per-prime step tables (primorial space).

sources.heading: 8.2 A pair wheel for the scan — with a caveat
sources.quote: a scan searching for twins need test only 25.8% of spoke positions — a 3.88× reduction in scan positions

nodes.name: Per-Prime Step Table Requires Primorial Space
nodes.statement: Restricting the advance stream to multipliers landing on pair-relevant positions requires a step table indexed by p mod W, i.e. primorial space, the obstruction of algorithm.md Remark 2.9.

clusters.name: Window Occupancy: Conjecture to Kernel Certificate
clusters.summary: Claim W begins as an open, hedged conjecture, is formalized into Lean definitions (which corrects it to exclude p=2), is checked computationally for primes below 60, and its implication to the twin prime conjecture is fully machine-checked.
